prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1483; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to keep my name off the record for now, but I can answer the questions.

Q: Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Baytown, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was light.

Q: Describe what happened right before the collision.
A: A car came over the center line and was coming straight at me. I braked and turned slightly to the right, but we still hit nearly head-on. It wasn't a high-speed crash. I'd say we were both going well under the posted limit, but the impact was enough to set off the airbags.

Q: Did you lose consciousness?
A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but everything went hazy for a few seconds. I remember my head snapping forward and then hitting the headrest.

Q: What symptoms did you notice in the days after?
A: The headache started within a few hours and didn't go away. I felt foggy, had trouble focusing on conversations, and light bothered my eyes. I also got dizzy when I stood up too quickly.

Q: Who did you see for treatment?
A: I went to the emergency room the same day. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. After that I saw my primary care doctor and was referred to a neurologist.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes. I have follow-up appointments and I do some vision and balance exercises with a therapist twice a week. My doctor told me the recovery could take a while.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I had to step back from work for several weeks. Reading for long periods is hard, and I get tired quickly. I used to coach my kid's soccer team and I had to hand that off to my spouse. I also stopped driving for a while because my reaction time felt off.

Q: Have your symptoms improved since the accident?
A: Some of them have. The headaches are less frequent now, but I still have bad days where the fog comes back, especially when I'm stressed or tired.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about your injuries?
A: Only that I'm doing what my doctors ask me to do. I want to get back to normal, and I'm working at it every day.
